title: View Through a Window May Influence Recovery from Surgery
tags: environmental psychology; healthcare design; stress recovery
short_summary: Retrospective matched study of postsurgical recovery records comparing patients with tree views against patients facing a brick wall; useful as a landmark source for restorative views, but narrow enough that claims should stay specific to recovery context.
notes: Use carefully: one hospital wing and a matched retrospective design.

title: The Restorative Benefits of Nature: Toward an Integrative Framework
tags: attention restoration; nature; directed attention
short_summary: Introduces Attention Restoration Theory as a framework for how environments can help recover directed attention; strong conceptual source for soft fascination and attention fatigue, especially when discussing natural features in designed space.
notes: Pair with empirical studies when making claims about outcomes.

title: The Free-Energy Principle: A Unified Brain Theory?
tags: predictive processing; active inference; perception-action
short_summary: Review article proposing free-energy minimisation as a unifying account of perception, action, learning, attention, and salience; useful for framing humans as active prediction systems coupled to their environments.
notes: Use as theoretical framing rather than direct evidence that specific rooms produce specific states.

title: Inner Vision: An Exploration of Art and the Brain
tags: neuroaesthetics; visual brain; art perception
short_summary: Foundational neuroaesthetics book connecting visual-brain specialization with aesthetic experience; useful for explaining why visual form, color, and composition can be treated as perceptual variables rather than decorative extras.
notes: Book source; pair with papers for specific neural claims.

title: The Aesthetic Brain: How We Evolved to Desire Beauty and Enjoy Art
tags: neuroaesthetics; beauty; perception
short_summary: Synthesizes neuroscience, psychology, and evolutionary arguments about beauty and aesthetic response; useful for keeping beauty claims grounded in empirical aesthetics rather than taste language alone.
notes: Book source; avoid treating aesthetic preference as universal without context.

title: Phototransduction by Retinal Ganglion Cells That Set the Circadian Clock
authors: David M. Berson; Felice A. Dunn; Motoharu Takao
tags: ipRGC; circadian clock; non-image-forming vision
short_summary: Showed that retinal ganglion cells innervating the suprachiasmatic nucleus can respond directly to light even when rod and cone input is blocked; this is a landmark source for biological lighting beyond image-forming vision.
notes: Use for ipRGC discovery and circadian phototransduction claims.

title: A Novel Human Opsin in the Inner Retina
tags: melanopsin; inner retina; nonvisual photoreception
short_summary: Identified melanopsin expression in human and mammalian inner retina, with localization suggesting a role in non-image-forming responses such as circadian regulation and melatonin suppression.
notes: Pair with Provencio 1998 when discussing initial melanopsin discovery.

title: Regulation of Mammalian Circadian Behavior by Non-rod, Non-cone, Ocular Photoreceptors
tags: circadian entrainment; non-rod non-cone photoreceptors; Russell Foster
short_summary: Demonstrated in mice that circadian photoentrainment can persist without rods and cones but is abolished by removing the eyes; useful for the claim that ocular light biology is not reducible to visual brightness.
notes: Use as pre-ipRGC evidence for an additional ocular photoreceptor system.

title: Melanopsin (Opn4) Requirement for Normal Light-Induced Circadian Phase Shifting
tags: melanopsin; circadian phase shifting; light exposure
short_summary: Showed that melanopsin contributes to normal circadian phase shifting responses to light; useful for separating strong circadian timing evidence from weaker claims about general mood or atmosphere.
notes: Use for light-induced phase shifting

title: CIE S 026/E:2018 CIE System for Metrology of Optical Radiation for ipRGC-Influenced Responses to Light
tags: lighting standards; melanopic measurement; ipRGC
short_summary: Defines quantities and spectral sensitivity functions for describing optical radiation that stimulates the five photoreceptor classes relevant to ipRGC-influenced responses; important for translating biology into lighting measurement.
notes: Standard does not predict specific health outcomes or prescribe application-level lighting recipes.

title: Measuring and Using Light in the Melanopsin Age
tags: melanopsin; light measurement; nonvisual responses
short_summary: Review and consensus-style guidance arguing that light should be specified in ways that account for melanopsin and other photoreceptor inputs, not only photopic lux; useful for design claims about measurement and specification.
notes: Use as a bridge source between laboratory biology and applied lighting practice.

title: From Sound to Movement: Mapping the Neural Mechanisms of Auditory-Motor Entrainment and Synchronization
authors: Marija Pranjic; Thenille Braun Janzen; Nikolina Vuksic; Michael Thaut
tags: auditory-motor entrainment; synchronization; neuroimaging
short_summary: Scoping review of neuroimaging studies on auditory-motor entrainment and synchronization; maps rhythm-to-movement networks including premotor, supplementary motor, basal ganglia, cerebellar, and prefrontal systems.
notes: Use as current overview; it synthesizes evidence rather than testing one studio-like intervention.

title: Rhythm Music and the Brain: Scientific Foundations and Clinical Applications
tags: neurologic music therapy; rhythmic entrainment; movement rehabilitation
short_summary: Foundational book for neurologic music therapy and rhythm-based motor rehabilitation; useful for explaining why rhythm can function as movement infrastructure rather than only entertainment.
notes: Book source; pair with clinical papers for specific outcome claims.

title: Rhythmic Auditory Stimulation in Gait Training for Parkinson's Disease Patients
tags: rhythmic auditory stimulation; gait; Parkinson disease
short_summary: Clinical gait-training study using rhythmic auditory stimulation in Parkinson disease; reports improvements in velocity, stride length, cadence, and gait timing after rhythm-paced training.
notes: Use for rehabilitation and cadence claims; avoid generalizing directly to healthy yoga participants.

title: Neurobiological Foundations of Neurologic Music Therapy: Rhythmic Entrainment and the Motor System
authors: Michael H. Thaut; Gerald C. McIntosh; Volker Hoemberg
tags: neurologic music therapy; motor system; rhythmic entrainment
short_summary: Review of rhythmic entrainment as a mechanism for neurologic music therapy, especially how auditory rhythm can couple with motor timing and support movement rehabilitation.
notes: Good bridge from clinical methods to neural mechanism.

title: Pulse and Meter as Neural Resonance
authors: Edward W. Large; Joel S. Snyder
journal_or_publisher: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
tags: neural resonance; pulse; meter; rhythm perception
short_summary: Theoretical neuroscience account proposing that pulse and meter perception can be understood through neural resonance; useful for framing rhythm as predictive temporal structure.
notes: Use as theory; pair with EEG/neuroimaging evidence for empirical claims.

title: Selective Neuronal Entrainment to the Beat and Meter Embedded in a Musical Rhythm
authors: Sylvie Nozaradan; Isabelle Peretz; Andre Mouraux
tags: EEG; beat perception; meter; neural entrainment
short_summary: EEG study showing enhanced neural responses at perceived beat and meter frequencies, even when those frequencies are not simply dominant in the acoustic signal; useful evidence that the brain constructs rhythmic structure.
notes: Use for beat/meter neural entrainment
column14: not all forms of social synchrony.

title: Treatise on Physiological Optics
journal_or_publisher: Leopold Voss; Optical Society of America
tags: unconscious inference; visual perception; historical lineage
short_summary: Historical anchor for unconscious inference: perception is treated as an active interpretive process rather than passive recording of sensory input.
notes: Historical source; use for lineage and conceptual ancestry rather than modern empirical evidence.

title: Surfing Uncertainty: Prediction, Action, and the Embodied Mind
tags: predictive processing; embodied cognition; action
short_summary: Major synthesis of predictive processing and embodied cognition, useful for framing perception, action, and bodily regulation as coupled prediction-error dynamics.
notes: Book source; pair with papers for specific neural or behavioral claims.

title: Being You: A New Science of Consciousness
tags: consciousness; controlled hallucination; selfhood
short_summary: Accessible synthesis of consciousness science that popularizes perception as controlled prediction while tying conscious selfhood to bodily and interoceptive processes.
notes: Trade book; useful for public-facing language but not a standalone empirical source.

title: Interoceptive inference, emotion, and the embodied self
tags: interoception; emotion; embodied self; predictive coding
short_summary: Extends predictive processing to interoception and emotion, arguing that embodied self-experience depends on inference about internal bodily causes as well as external sensory causes.
notes: Strong bridge source for breath/body-awareness language; keep intervention claims modest.

title: Predictions not commands: active inference in the motor system
authors: Rick A. Adams; Stewart Shipp; Karl J. Friston
tags: active inference; motor control; proprioception; prediction
short_summary: Review proposing that motor control can be understood through active inference: actions fulfil proprioceptive predictions rather than merely executing top-down commands.
notes: Useful for movement sequencing and proprioceptive prediction framing; avoid implying it directly tests yoga practice.

title: Multisensory integration: current issues from the perspective of the single neuron
authors: Barry E. Stein; Terrence R. Stanford
tags: multisensory integration; sensory congruence; neural integration
short_summary: Review of how neurons combine inputs across senses, including spatial and temporal constraints on when multisensory signals enhance or interfere with perception and action.
notes: Use for general multisensory coherence; not direct evidence about yoga-studio ambience.

title: Cognitive Load During Problem Solving: Effects on Learning
tags: cognitive load; working memory; schema acquisition; instructional design
short_summary: Foundational cognitive-load paper arguing that problem-solving formats can consume working-memory resources that would otherwise support learning and schema formation.
notes: Useful for reducing unnecessary complexity in cues/interfaces; translate carefully from learning tasks to studio design.

title: Distracted and confused?: Selective attention under load
tags: attention; distraction; perceptual load; cognitive control
short_summary: Review of load theory showing that perceptual and cognitive load shape how well people filter distractors and maintain selective attention.
notes: Good support for attentional friction language; avoid treating all load as harmful.

title: The flow experience and its significance for human psychology
tags: flow; optimal experience; attention; challenge-skill balance
short_summary: Foundational flow chapter describing flow as deep task absorption shaped by clear goals, feedback, concentration, intrinsic reward, and the relation between challenge and skill.
notes: Use as foundational theory; pair with newer neuroscience and measurement work for biological claims.

title: The cognitive neuroscience of insight
tags: insight; Aha experience; creativity; cognitive neuroscience
short_summary: Review synthesizing behavioral and neural work on insight problem solving, including preparation, unconscious processing, neural precursors, and Aha experience.
notes: Use for insight and creative-cognition framing; do not collapse insight into flow.

title: Aha! Insight experience correlates with solution activation in the right hemisphere
tags: Aha experience; right hemisphere; semantic activation; insight problem solving
short_summary: Experimental insight paper showing that reported Aha experiences correlate with solution-related activation patterns, supporting the idea that solutions can be partly activated before conscious report.
notes: Useful for preconscious-idea language; avoid overstating hemispheric specialization.

title: Creative flow as optimized processing: Evidence from brain oscillations during jazz improvisations by expert and non-expert musicians
authors: David Rosen; Yongtaek Oh; Christine Chesebrough; Fengqing Zoe Zhang; John Kounios
tags: creative flow; EEG; jazz improvisation; expertise
short_summary: EEG study of jazz guitar improvisation linking higher flow and expertise with reduced frontal/executive activity and greater posterior/central activity, consistent with optimized processing in skilled creative performance.
notes: Strong flow-neuroscience source; limited to a specific creative-expertise task and not a universal biomarker.

title: Lecons Sur Les Phenomenes de la Vie Communs Aux Animaux Et Aux Vegetaux
tags: physiology; internal environment; regulation
short_summary: Historical lectures associated with Bernard's internal-environment framing; useful as lineage for later homeostasis and allostasis concepts rather than as modern experimental evidence.
notes: Historical source; pair with Sterling and contemporary physiology for current claims.

title: Allostasis: A model of predictive regulation
tags: allostasis; predictive regulation; physiology
short_summary: Review framing allostasis as predictive regulation: the brain anticipates needs, prioritizes resources, and adjusts bodily parameters efficiently rather than defending rigid set points.
notes: Strong conceptual bridge for regulation language; does not prove specific room or class designs directly regulate physiology.

title: The Ecological Approach to Visual Perception
tags: affordances; ecological psychology; perception-action
short_summary: Classic ecological-perception source emphasizing that environments are perceived in relation to possible action; useful for translating design features into affordances for movement and attention.
notes: Theory source; use for perception-action framing

title: Potential self-regulatory mechanisms of yoga for psychological health
authors: Tim Gard; Jessica J. Noggle; Crystal L. Park; David R. Vago; Angela Wilson
tags: yoga; self-regulation; psychological health; interoception
short_summary: Review proposing self-regulatory pathways through which yoga may affect psychological health, including attention control, emotion regulation, body awareness, and stress physiology.
notes: Mechanistic review; keep claims about specific breathing practices or class designs conditional unless supported by direct trials.

title: The Quiet Eye: Origins Controversies and Future Directions
tags: quiet eye; gaze control; expert performance; attention
short_summary: Review of Quiet Eye research tracing how final fixations before movement relate to expertise, decision making, and motor performance across sport and skilled action contexts.
notes: Useful for gaze and attentional timing; translate carefully into yoga teaching rather than treating it as direct class evidence.

title: Motor Learning
authors: John W. Krakauer; Adrian M. Hadjiosif; Jing Xu; Aaron L. Wong; Adrian M. Haith
tags: motor learning; adaptation; skill; feedback
short_summary: Comprehensive review of motor learning mechanisms, including adaptation, skill acquisition, feedback, practice, memory, and transfer.
notes: Strong general motor-learning source; use to design teaching hypotheses
column14: not to claim one cueing method is proven for yoga.

title: Ecological Dynamics: A Theoretical Framework for Understanding Sport Performance Physical Education and Physical Activity
journal_or_publisher: First Complex Systems Digital Campus World E-Conference 2015
tags: ecological dynamics; constraints-led approach; skill acquisition; practice design
short_summary: Theoretical chapter framing skill learning as a person-task-environment system shaped by constraints, affordances, variability, and representative practice.
notes: Good bridge for teaching environment and cue design; keep claims about studio outcomes as applied hypotheses.

title: Approaching awe a moral spiritual and aesthetic emotion
tags: awe; vastness; accommodation; aesthetic emotion
used_in: Article 1; Article 10; The Neuroscience of Awe
short_summary: Foundational paper defining awe around perceived vastness and a need for accommodation, with moral, spiritual, natural, and aesthetic variants.
notes: Use to distinguish awe from beauty and flow; it is a theory-building paper rather than a design intervention.

title: Awe the small self and prosocial behavior
authors: Paul K. Piff; Pia Dietze; Matthew Feinberg; Daniel M. Stancato; Dacher Keltner
journal_or_publisher: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
tags: awe; small self; prosocial behavior; emotion
short_summary: Multi-study paper linking awe experiences with a smaller self-focus and more prosocial tendencies, useful for grounding awe as more than aesthetic pleasure.
notes: Use carefully: social/emotional outcomes should not be generalized to every beautiful environment.

title: Distributed cognition: toward a new foundation for human-computer interaction research
authors: James Hollan; Edwin Hutchins; David Kirsh
tags: distributed cognition; HCI; cognitive systems; tools
short_summary: Argues that human-computer interaction should be understood across whole environments where cognition is distributed among people, artifacts, tools, representations, and activity over time.
notes: Strong product-theory source; pair with user research before claiming a specific interface becomes invisible.
